study_overview.study_purpose: To assess if treatment with veliparib plus carboplatin and paclitaxel results in improved survival compared to Investigator's choice of standard chemotherapy in Lung Subtype Panel (LSP) positive subjects with metastatic or advanced Non-Squamous Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer (NSCLC).
study_overview.study_duration_for_participant: Participants will receive treatment for a maximum of 6 cycles (each 21 days). After treatment, they will have follow-up visits every 9-12 weeks and survival status will be monitored every 2 months until disease progression, death, or the study ends.
study_overview.study_locations: This is a multicenter study with approximately 150 study sites.

provenance.text_snippet:
The primary objective of the study is to assess if treatment with veliparib plus carboplatin and paclitaxel results in improved survival compared to Investigator's choice of standard chemotherapy in Lung Subtype Panel (LSP) positive subjects with metastatic or advanced NSCLC.
Number of Subjects to be Enrolled: 595
Study Sites: 150

treatment_procedures.description: Taking veliparib capsules by mouth twice a day for 7 consecutive days, and receiving carboplatin and paclitaxel by intravenous (IV) infusion on Day 1 of each 21-day cycle.
treatment_procedures.frequency: Each 21-day cycle, for up to 6 cycles

provenance.text_snippet: Veliparib 120 mg BID Days –2 through 5; carboplatin AUC 6 mg/mL•min administered on Day 1; and paclitaxel 200 mg/m2 administered on Day 1 of each 21-day cycle;

treatment_procedures.description: Receiving Investigator's choice of standard platinum doublet chemotherapy by IV infusion on Day 1 of each 21-day cycle.
treatment_procedures.frequency: Each 21-day cycle, for up to 6 cycles

treatment_procedures.description: Suitable subjects may receive pemetrexed maintenance therapy after completing the initial 6 cycles of chemotherapy.
treatment_procedures.frequency: Day 1 of each 21-day cycle after initial treatment

provenance.text_snippet: Maintenance therapy after completion of up to 6 cycles of either veliparib/carboplatin/paclitaxel or Investigator's choice of chemotherapy. Maintenance therapy consists of pemetrexed or no maintenance therapy (observational).

follow_up_procedures.description: After stopping treatment, you will have follow-up visits with physical exams, vital signs, and lab tests.
follow_up_procedures.frequency: Every 9 weeks for the first year, then every 12 weeks.

provenance.text_snippet: After cessation of therapy, physician visits and quality of life measures will be performed q9 weeks until 1 year after beginning treatment (C1D-2) (or beyond 1 year until maintenance therapy is discontinued), then q12 weeks until radiographic progression.

follow_up_procedures.description: CT scans to monitor your cancer.
follow_up_procedures.frequency: Every 9 weeks for the first year, then every 12 weeks until disease progression or death.

provenance.text_snippet: After cessation of platinum doublet therapy, tumor assessments will be performed q9 weeks until 1 year after beginning treatment (C1D-2) (or beyond 1 year until maintenance therapy is discontinued), then q12 weeks until radiographic progression or death.

follow_up_procedures.description: The study team will contact you or check public records to see how you are doing.
follow_up_procedures.frequency: At 2-month intervals after clinical assessments stop.

provenance.text_snippet: Subjects no longer undergoing clinical assessments will have survival information reported at 2-month intervals (or as requested by the sponsor to support data analysis) beginning at the last clinical assessment and continuing until the endpoint of death...

optional_procedures.description: One 4 mL whole blood sample will be collected for DNA isolation to study how your genes may affect your response to the study drug. This requires a separate informed consent.

provenance.text_snippet: One 4 mL whole blood sample for DNA isolation will be collected on C1D-2 from each subject who consents to provide a sample for pharmacogenetic analysis. known_risks.risk_description: Neutropenia (low white blood cell count), which can increase risk of infection.
known_risks.management: Monitoring of blood counts, dose adjustments, and use of growth factors if needed.

provenance.text_snippet: The most common AEs reported in this study were neutropenia and fatigue (reported in > 50% of subjects)...

known_risks.risk_description: Thrombocytopenia (low platelet count), which can increase risk of bleeding.
known_risks.management: Monitoring of blood counts and dose adjustments.

provenance.text_snippet: ...nausea, thrombocytopenia, and peripheral sensory neuropathy (> 40% of subjects)...

known_risks.management: Monitoring of blood counts, potential for blood transfusions.

provenance.text_snippet: ...and anemia, constipation, alopecia, diarrhea, decreased appetite, lymphopenia, and myalgia (> 20% of subjects).

known_risks.risk_description: Other common side effects include constipation, alopecia (hair loss), diarrhea, decreased appetite, and muscle pain (myalgia).
known_risks.management: Supportive care and management of symptoms.

provenance.text_snippet: ...and anemia, constipation, alopecia, diarrhea, decreased appetite, lymphopenia, and myalgia (> 20% of subjects).

known_risks.management: Premedication is given to reduce the risk. Close monitoring during infusion.

provenance.text_snippet: Main toxicities associated with the use of paclitaxel include myelosuppression, neuropathy and hypersensitivity reactions.

potential_risks: Changes in testes or ovaries affecting fertility
risks.reproductive_risks: The study drugs can harm a developing fetus. Female participants must not become pregnant and male participants must not father a child during the study and for a period after.
risks.unknown_risks_statement: There may be other risks from the study treatment that are not yet known.
risks.risk_mitigation_measures: You will be monitored closely for side effects. Doses of the study drugs may be delayed, reduced, or stopped to manage toxicities. Supportive care and medications will be provided as needed.

provenance.text_snippet: Risks in this study include toxicity from the addition of veliparib to standard therapy. ... Other potential risks of veliparib administration, identified in preclinical studies or based on pharmacological mechanism, but not confirmed in clinical studies must also be considered. These risks include seizures, changes in testes/ovaries, toxicity to the developing fetus and secondary malignancies.

potential_benefits: The addition of veliparib to standard chemotherapy may improve clinical outcomes, such as survival, for subjects with advanced NSCLC.
benefits.no_benefit_statement: There is no guarantee that you will receive any direct medical benefit from participating in this study. Your condition may not improve or may worsen.
benefits.societal_benefits: The information learned from this study may help to establish improved clinical outcomes for future subjects with advanced NSCLC.

provenance.text_snippet: This study proposes to establish improved clinical outcomes for subjects with advanced NSCLC through the addition of veliparib to standard therapy with carboplatin and paclitaxel.

alternative_treatments.description: You can receive standard first-line chemotherapy for NSCLC outside of this study. This includes various platinum-doublet combinations.
You may be eligible to participate in other research studies.

alternatives.standard_of_care_description: The standard first-line treatment for metastatic non-small cell lung cancer includes a platinum-containing chemotherapy combination. The control arm of this study uses this standard of care.

provenance.text_snippet: National Comprehensive Cancer Network (NCCN) 2014 guidelines3 and ESMO guidelines4 recommend that first-line treatment with cytotoxic chemotherapy for metastatic non-small cell lung cancer should include a platinum combination.

compensation_costs.travel_reimbursement: For subjects in Japan, transportation expenses will be paid to lighten the burden of participation.
covered_costs: The investigational drug (veliparib) and the chemotherapy drugs used in the study will be provided by the sponsor.
compensation_costs.injury_compensation: For subjects in Japan, if you suffer a health impairment related to the study drug, the sponsor will cover medical expenses not covered by health insurance. The sponsor has clinical study insurance to cover claims and compensation.

confidentiality.data_protection_statement: Information received or developed in connection with this protocol will be kept confidential. Your personal information will be protected, and if study results are published, you will not be identified.
who_has_access: The study team at the site
Institutional Review Boards (IRB) or Independent Ethics Committees (IEC)
confidentiality.data_retention_period: DNA samples collected for optional pharmacogenetic research will be stored for up to 20 years.
confidentiality.data_sharing: Aggregate (grouped) information from this study may be used in scientific publications or presented at medical conventions. De-identified data from optional genetic research may be used for future research.

provenance.text_snippet: Aggregate pharmacogenetic information from this study may be used in scientific publications or presented at medical conventions. Pharmacogenetic information will be published or presented only in a way that does not identify any individual subject.

voluntary_participation.voluntary_statement: Participation in this study is voluntary. You can decide not to participate or to leave the study at any time.
voluntary_participation.withdrawal_rights: You have the right to withdraw from study treatment at any time for any reason, without penalty or loss of benefits to which you are otherwise entitled.
voluntary_participation.withdrawal_consequences: If you decide to withdraw, the study doctor will discuss this with you. You may be asked to complete a final study visit for safety reasons.
voluntary_participation.data_after_withdrawal: Data collected up to the point of your withdrawal may still be used in the study analysis to protect the integrity of the research.

provenance.text_snippet: Each subject has the right to withdraw from study treatment at any time. In addition, the Investigator may discontinue a subject from the study treatment at any time for any reason if the Investigator considers it necessary...

genetic_testing.description: An optional blood sample can be provided for pharmacogenetic analysis. This research will look at your DNA to learn about genetic factors that may contribute to the disease or your response to treatment.
genetic_testing.results_disclosure: Individual results from this research will not be given to you, your doctor, or anyone not directly involved in the research.

provenance.text_snippet: Pharmacogenetic analysis will only be performed if the subject has voluntarily signed and dated a separate pharmacogenetic informed consent, approved by an IRB/IEC...

AbbVie will store the DNA samples in a secure storage space with adequate measures to protect confidentiality. The samples will be retained while research on ABT-888 (or drugs of this class) continues but no longer than 20 years.

reproductive_requirements.contraception_requirements: Female subjects of childbearing potential and their male partners, as well as male subjects and their female partners of childbearing potential, must agree to use at least one of the specified methods of birth control.
reproductive_requirements.contraception_duration: During the study and for at least 6 months after the last treatment with chemotherapy.
reproductive_requirements.pregnancy_reporting: If you or your partner become pregnant during the study, you must inform the study doctor immediately.
reproductive_requirements.breastfeeding_restrictions: Subjects who are pregnant or lactating are not allowed to participate in the study.
reproductive_requirements.male_requirements: Male subjects must use a specified method of birth control with their female partners of childbearing potential.
